note: Our values recomputed over the same period as each study. Sources are peer-reviewed papers or agency publications; directions all agree, sizes are compared honestly.

rows.ours: +1.08 °C per decade (95 % range +0.74 to +1.59), 1991–2018, NASA POWER cell
rows.published: +1.7 °C per decade since 1991 at the Svalbard Airport station
rows.explanation: Same direction and exceptional size, but about a third lower: the ~55 km grid cell mixes land, sea and glacier, while the study uses one station.

rows.published: −8.6 (1981–2004) and about −9 W/m² per decade at Indian stations
rows.source: Padma Kumari et al. (2007), as cited in Soni et al., ACP preprint acp-2017-429
rows.explanation: Close agreement with the station-based dimming estimates.

rows.published: −2.9 ± 1.9 W/m² per decade, CERES average over all of India, 2001–2018
rows.source: IIT Delhi study (summary by Saur Energy)
rows.explanation: Same direction; stronger in Delhi than the all-India average, plausible for one of the most aerosol-polluted cities.

rows.source: Government of Western Australia, citing the Bureau of Meteorology
rows.explanation: Same direction; ours is larger. The periods and baseline differ (two 15-year windows against a long pre-1975 baseline).

rows.ours: Getting wetter since 1981, significant (NASA POWER); ERA5 shows almost no trend
rows.published: Partial recovery since the 1980s drought, still below 1950s levels
rows.explanation: Agrees with the published partial recovery; the two reanalyses disagree on its size (see the ERA5 check).
